extDesc.message: Bilingual subtitles for YouTube — original and translation in one non-overlapping layer.

disclaimer.message: Not affiliated with YouTube or Google.

provTtsZhReco.description: Suffix chip on the Alibaba Qwen-TTS provider entry when the TARGET language is Chinese: its Mandarin/dialect voices are the reason to pick it.

provOllama.description: Provider list: the Ollama preset, a model server on the user's own machine. Keep "Ollama"; translate only the word in brackets.

backendTipHtml.message:
Auto: uses YouTube's whole-track translation whenever the video supports it, and switches to smart sentences when it doesn't.
Whole-track: YouTube's own translation; aligned cue for cue. Heavy use can make YouTube rate-limit it briefly — the extension waits and asks again.
Smart sentences: rebuilds fragmented captions into whole sentences, then translates them through Google's free endpoint — better wording than whole-track on messy tracks, but heavy use can be rate-limited there too; the extension slows down and retries.
Own key: sends the assembled sentence to the provider you configured.

backendGtxHint.message: Uses Google's free endpoint — heavy use may be briefly rate-limited; the extension paces itself and retries automatically.

backendStatusLimited.message: Rate-limited by the translation endpoint — slowing down and retrying automatically. Already-translated lines keep working.

diagCopied.message: Copied — paste it into an email or issue

diagCopyFail.message: Copy failed — take a screenshot instead

backendStatusSame.message: This video's subtitles are already in your translation language — nothing to translate.

backendStatusNoTrack.message: No caption track was found for this video, so there is nothing to show.
backendStatusNoTrack.description: Popup: the engine status line when the page reported that the video has no caption track at all (the commonest support question).

backendStatusNoVideo.message: Open a YouTube video and the two lines appear on it. If you are already on one, reload the tab.

posHint.message: You can also drag the subtitle box on the video

resetConfirmText.message: This clears every setting, the API keys saved on this computer, and the model and voice remembered for each provider, and turns the first-run hints back on. Provider domains you have already granted stay granted, and so do the font files you imported.
resetConfirmText.description: Popup: the inline panel that opens when 'Reset all settings' is pressed. Says exactly what a reset clears.

resetConfirmBack.description: Popup: the safe button on the reset panel — closes it, changes nothing.

resetConfirmGo.description: Popup: the destructive button on the reset panel — performs the reset.

handleTitle.message: Drag to move · double-click to reset

handleAria.message: Drag to move subtitles, double-click to reset

exportNoTrans.message: No translation available for this video — try the Whole-track engine or another translation language.

exportLimited.message: YouTube is rate-limiting whole-track translation right now — try again in a minute. Switch Engine to Your own key and the export card offers a tick that goes around it.

exportNoCues.message: No downloadable subtitles — play a few seconds so captions load, then try again.

exportNotYoutube.message: Open a YouTube video page to export.

exportFailed.message: Export failed — refresh the page and try again.

trackWarnDubOnly.message: Heads up: this video only has AI-dubbed auto captions (no original-language track), so the bilingual subtitles may not match the audio.

backendStatusByoUnset.message: Your own key is not set up yet, so nothing is being translated. Use “Configure…” below to set it up.

byoSiteHint.message: Pick the site you signed up on — the two are separate platforms and a key from one is not accepted by the other.

byoKeyCleared.message: The key stored on this machine has been deleted.

byoKeyClearedMoved.message: The key stored on this machine has been deleted. That one was in use, so translation now goes through $NAME$.

byoLocalHint.message: The key is kept in this browser, on this machine, and is not synced to your account. It goes to one place: the provider you picked, as the authorization header on each request — and so does the subtitle text.

byoErrNoKey.message: Enter an API key first, then press Save and test.

byoErrNoModel.message: Pick a model first — choose one from the list, or press “List models with my key”.

byoErrNoModelEmpty.message: This provider ships no list. Fetch the available models first, or type the model name yourself.

byoErrNotApi.message: That address answered with a web page, not the API — usually a sign-in wall or a network that intercepts requests. Check the address, or try another network.

byoErrBadBaseUrl.message: The API base URL needs the whole address, starting with https:// — http:// works only for localhost and 127.0.0.1.

byoErrUrlHasKey.message: The address has a key in it. Take it out of the address and paste it into the API key field — the address is synced to your browser account, the key field is not.

byoErrNoPerm.message: Without permission to reach that API host the extension cannot connect. Press “Save and test” again and allow it.

byoErrAuth.message: The key was rejected (401) — check that it was copied in full and is still active.

byoErrForbiddenLocal.message: The server on this machine refused the call (403). It has most likely not been told to allow the extension: OLLAMA_ORIGINS for Ollama, the CORS switch in LM Studio.

byoErrForbidden.message: The provider refused this call (403). Usually the key is fine and the account is not allowed to make it — an unpaid balance, an identity check still pending, a model not switched on, or the region. Check the account in the provider's console.

byoErrListAuth.message: This key isn't allowed to read the list. Give it that permission in the provider's dashboard, then fetch again.
byoErrListAuth.description: Shown when fetching a model/voice LIST is refused with 401/403. Different from byoErrAuth on purpose: the key already works for synthesis, so the refusal is about per-endpoint permissions (ElevenLabs keys can allow Text to Speech but not Voices).

byoErrLimited.message: The provider is rate-limiting — slowing down and retrying automatically.

byoErrLimitedTest.message: The provider is rate-limiting. Wait a moment and press it again.

byoErrQuota.message: This account is out of credit or quota for the current period — top it up in the provider's console to carry on.

byoErrBadRequest.message: The endpoint refused the request — the model name or base URL may be wrong.

byoErrBadShape.message: The model did not answer line by line as asked, and smaller retries failed too — try another model.

byoErrReasoning.message: That model returned only its chain of thought and no translation — pick a non-thinking model.

byoErrNetfail.message: Cannot reach that endpoint (network or regional restriction).

byoErrNetfailLocal.message: Cannot reach that address: either the server is not running, or it has not been told to allow the extension (OLLAMA_ORIGINS for Ollama, the CORS switch in LM Studio).

byoErrUnsupportedTarget.message: This provider cannot translate into your chosen language — change the language or the engine.

byoErrFailed.message: Connection failed. Try again in a moment.

optIntro.message: Pick a provider and paste your own API key.

optModelRetired.message: “$MODEL$” is no longer on this provider's list — pick another one above.

optModelsFailed.message: Could not list models — type the model name instead.

optNoModelsYet.message: No model list yet — fetch one with your key, or just type the name.

optNoModelsYetNoKey.message: No model list yet — fetch one, or just type the name.

optModelEndpointId.message: This provider wants the endpoint ID from its own console — the shape shown above — not a public model name.

optAfterSetup.message: When you are done here, open the extension popup and set Engine to "Your own key".

optTrademark.message: All provider names and logos are trademarks of their respective owners. This extension is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by any of them; the marks are shown only to identify the API you picked.

startIntro.message: Four things. You do not have to set anything up to use it.

startS1Body.message: Any YouTube video that has subtitles: the two lines appear on their own.

startS2Body.message: Hold the grip at the top-left of the subtitle box and drag it anywhere. Double-click the grip to put it back.

startS2Alt.message: Player diagram: a six-dot grip at the top-left corner of the subtitle box, dragging it to another position

startS3Body.message: Add your own API key: whole-sentence translation, and whole-video translation when you export.

aboutIntro.message: What this is, and where your text goes.

uiLocaleHint.message: The language of this extension's own menus and settings. A few labels drawn on the video itself still follow the browser's language. The translation language is chosen in the popup; the “Translation languages” pane only decides which languages the popup lists.

cmdToggleTransLine.message: Show or hide the translation line

optShortcutsHint.message: Chrome keeps these keys, not the extension. Nothing is bound to begin with; three things can be: subtitles on/off, read aloud on/off, and show or hide the translation line.

optShortcutsFallback.message: Chrome would not open that page from here — paste chrome://extensions/shortcuts into the address bar.

startTargetHint.message: Guessed from your browser's language preferences when the extension was installed. Change it here if the guess is wrong — the popup can change it any time.

aboutBlurb.message: A second subtitle line for YouTube: the original on one line, the translation on the other, with the font, colour and position up to you. Open source, free, no ads.

aboutPrivacy.message: The extension has no server of ours and collects no statistics. Subtitle text goes only to services you chose: the translation service you pick and, if you turn them on, the speech provider for read-aloud and the provider you set up for summaries. With your own key, the key is stored on this computer only.

popupSummarize.description: Popup, under the provider row: opens the summary panel in the player. The panel says which provider it will use and what it will cost before anything is sent.

exportUsesYouTube.message: The download uses YouTube's own whole-track translation — free, and it does not spend your API key.

exportUseByo.message: Translate with my own key (closer match, spends quota)

exportByoNote.message: The whole track will be translated by your provider with your key. You will see an estimate before anything is sent.

exportConfirm.message: Translate $N$ subtitle lines with $NAME$ — roughly $REQ$ requests against your own quota. The whole track leaves your browser for that provider; during playback only the parts you actually watch are ever sent.

exportPartial.message: $N$ chunk(s) fell back to YouTube's translation

ftFeedback.message: Send feedback or report a bug

ftReview.message: Rate it on the Chrome Web Store

optNeedKey.message: No key yet — this provider cannot be used until you add one.

optNeedBase.message: No endpoint address yet — this provider cannot be used until you enter one.

optBaseHint.message: Either the base URL or the full endpoint works, e.g. https://example.com/v1 or https://example.com/v1/chat/completions. A model server on this machine takes the port that server uses — http://localhost:11434/v1 for Ollama, http://localhost:1234/v1 for LM Studio. The key can be left empty; http is only allowed for loopback addresses.

startS1Alt.message: Player diagram: an original line and a translated line sit near the bottom of the picture

startS3Alt.message: Comparison: the free engine translates one sentence in pieces, your own key understands it whole and splits it back

startS4Title.message: There's a little menu in the player

startS4Body.message: The small arrow next to the subtitle button opens a menu: subtitles, read aloud, select text, video summary and settings — without leaving the player.

startS4Alt.message: Player illustration: a small arrow next to the subtitle button, bottom right, opens a small menu

menuHintBubble.message: Read aloud, video summary, select text — all behind this little arrow

troubleStep1.message: Check the switch in the popup first — with it off, the whole subtitle layer stays away.

troubleStep2.message: Does this video have subtitles at all? Try the CC button in the player: without an original there is nothing to translate.

troubleStep3.message: Try a popular video. If everything else works and only this one does not, it is usually this video's subtitle track.

troubleDiagHint.message: Still stuck? Paste the diagnostic info into your email or issue — it carries the version, the engine state and what the current tab is doing, which saves a round trip or two.

ttsIntro.message: Read the translated line out loud. Your browser's own voices need no key at all; the cloud providers are set up and tested here.

ttsPreviewFail.message: Could not play — check the key and try Save and test

ttsFetchVoices.message: Fetch this language's full list with your key

ttsVoicesSwitched.message: These are all $N$ voices your key has for the current language, older Standard / Wavenet tiers included. They only apply to this language; click the line above to go back to the everyday voices, which follow you across languages. You can fetch this list again any time.

ttsBackToFamily.message: Back to the everyday voices (they follow the language)

ttsVoicesNone.message: This provider has no extra voices for this language — the built-in ones still work.

ttsVoicesSuggested.message: Fetched $N$ voices — they are suggestions under the field above.

ttsPrivacyNote.message: Most of your browser's own voices are installed on this computer and speak the line here. A few are not: Chrome also offers online voices — the ones whose names begin with "Google" — and for those the browser sends the line to its maker. With a cloud provider, the text to be spoken goes only to the provider you chose, and the key stays on this machine.

ttsEnableLabel.message: Read the translation aloud in the video

ttsEnableHint.message: When on, each subtitle's translation is spoken as it appears; a line whose translation isn't ready in time is skipped rather than caught up on later. While a line speaks, the video's own audio drops to the level set below. A line that runs long slows the picture a little and borrows the gap after it — with cloud voices and with the browser's own; the switch below keeps slowing so more of them finish.

langsIntro.message: Which translation languages the popup offers.

langsKeptHint.message: These appear in the popup's translation-language menu. Keep at least one.

langsMoreHint.message: Press + to add one. The list follows the translation languages the free engines and DeepL support.

langsAllAdded.message: Every language is already in your list.

langsSwitched.message: That one was in use, so the translation language is now $NAME$

ttsErrNoRegion.message: Enter the service region of your Azure key first (e.g. eastus).

ttsNoSynth.message: This computer has no voices to speak with.

ttsNoVoiceForLang.message: This computer has no voice that reads $NAME$. The list below is other languages' voices — pick one and the line will be read with that language's accent.

ttsErrRefused.message: The provider refused this request — try a different voice.

ttsErrNoAudio.message: The audio did not come through — try again, or pick a different voice.

startPicChop1.description: Demo of a BAD chopped translation of 'there's two big' — keep it a broken half-sentence aligned to that English line. Never the fox demo.

startPicChop2.description: Demo of a BAD chopped translation of 'reasons one is' — keep it a broken half-sentence aligned to that English line. Never the fox demo.

startPicWhole1.description: First half of a GOOD whole-sentence translation of 'There are two big reasons,' — must connect into the next key. Never the fox demo.

startPicWhole2.description: Second half: 'the first one is…' — continues startPicWhole1. Never the fox demo.

ttsRobotVoices.description: Heading over the OS's machine/novelty voice pack at the bottom of the local-voice picker. Keep it to one short word.

selectTextLabel.message: Let me select and copy subtitle text
selectTextLabel.description: Checkbox in the popup layout card. When on, the two subtitle lines accept the mouse so their text can be selected and copied; clicks on them then no longer pause the video.

menuSelectText.description: Player-menu row label (short NAME, not a sentence). Toggles whether subtitle lines can be selected; clicking it copies nothing.

menuSummary.description: Player-menu action row: opens the in-player video summary panel.

sumPanelTitle.description: Title of the in-player summary panel.

sumClose.description: aria-label of the summary panel's close button.

sumEmpty.message: This video has no usable subtitle track.
sumEmpty.description: Summary panel: the video has no subtitle track to summarize.

sumNeedSubs.message: Turn the subtitles back on to summarize — the summary is built from the subtitle track.

sumNeedKey.message: Summaries need a service of your own: any provider with your key in the Translation service pane, or a local model on this machine. The free engines only translate. They don't summarize.
sumNeedKey.description: Summary panel empty state: summaries need a BYO-key or local-endpoint provider.

sumConfigure.description: Summary panel empty state: the primary button that opens the settings page. Same wording as startGoSetup (a primary action, no ellipsis), kept as its own key so the onboarding step and this panel can drift apart on purpose.

sumStart.description: Summary panel: the button that starts the (quota-burning) run.

sumFail.message: The summary failed. Try again later.

sumConfirm.message: This will send the whole subtitle track to $PROVIDER$, in $PARTS$ part(s), on your own quota.
sumConfirm.description: Summary panel confirm line before anything is sent. $PROVIDER$ = provider name, $PARTS$ = chunk count.

sumWorking.description: Summary panel progress line. $DONE$/$TOTAL$ = chunk counters.

sumFailedPart.message: $N$ part(s) could not be summarized; the rest is above.
sumFailedPart.description: Summary panel: some chunks failed. $N$ = how many.

menuSubtitles.description: Row label in the small in-player menu. One word.

tlangLimitedNote.message: YouTube's own translation is rate-limited right now; smart sentences (Google) is filling in. It retries by itself later.
tlangLimitedNote.description: Status line under the engine picker when auto fell back to gtx because YouTube's own translation endpoint is rate-limiting. Explains WHY, promises the automatic retry. No absolute claims.

exportWaiting.message: The translation endpoint is rate-limiting — resuming in about $SECONDS$ s.

optTtsBaseHint.message: A base URL or a full endpoint both work, e.g. http://localhost:8880/v1 or http://localhost:8880/v1/audio/speech (local speech servers like Kokoro or openai-edge-tts). The key may stay empty; plain http works only for loopback addresses.

optTtsNeedUrl.message: No endpoint address yet — this provider can't be used until you add one.

ttsSkipNotSet.message: not set up on this computer

ttsProviderMute.message: $NAME$ can't speak right now. Pick another in the row above — your browser's own voices are in that list.

statusTrackRetry.message: The subtitle track hasn't arrived — retrying automatically. In a hurry? Refresh the page to try again now.

ttsCompleteLabel.message: Try to finish every line (the picture slows in dense parts)

ttsCompleteHint.message: At higher speeds long lines often lose their tail to the next one. With this on, the picture slows as much as the line needs — never below a quarter of your chosen speed — and catches back up in the gaps. While the picture is slowed that deep, the video's own audio drops further than the level you set, down to silence.

ttsCompleteHintText.message: Quite a few lines are being cut short at this speed. Turn it on and the picture slows where it needs to, so more of them finish.

fontsIntro.message: One list serves both subtitle lines; the popup picks per line. Every font listed is installed on this computer.

fontsOnly.message: Only fonts that can draw it

fontsKeptEmpty.message: Only System default is left for the popup.
fontsKeptEmpty.description: Shown in the kept column of the fonts page when every font was removed from it.

fontsAllAdded.message: Every font is already in the list.

fontsUnavailable.message: This browser does not let the extension read the installed fonts, so only System default can be picked.

fontsImportHint.message: .ttf / .otf / .woff / .woff2; the file is copied into the browser.

fontsImportStore.message: Could not save it in the browser; try again.
fontsImportStore.description: Settings page: the font file was read but the browser refused to store the copy (IndexedDB quota or failure).

fontsRemoved.description: Settings page, fonts: status after pressing × on a kept font. $NAME$ = the font name.

fontsSkipList.description: Settings page, fonts: a keyboard-only link before each long font list that jumps past it.

fontImported.description: Name shown for an imported font whose record is not on this computer (synced from another machine, or deleted).

fontsImportBad.message: That is not a font file this browser can use.

fontsImportTooBig.message: The file is too large (limit $MB$ MB).
